Subject: Sizing kickoff — Atlas inference footprint (flash sale / holiday burst)

Hi Ava,

Thanks for taking this on. Quick context: Atlas is preparing for a multi-hour flash sale event where we expect a sharp spike in search traffic (product search + personalization reranking) and an increase in chat volume for the storefront assistant. High-level numbers from the product team:

- Typical steady-state QPS: ~120–200 requests/sec (mix of embeddings + generative chat + rerank)
- Expected peak flash sale QPS: sustained ~1,800 req/s for 8–12 minutes at the top of each hour across the 3-hour window; some bursts up to ~3,200 req/s for 30–60s
- Concurrency (inference in-flight requests) observed during spikes: 180–350 depending on model and batching strategy
- Prompt token distribution: median 28 tokens, 75th pct 60, 95th pct 220
- Response tokens: median 64, typical upper bound we allow is 512 tokens for certain templated responses
- Workloads:
  - Reranking (encoder/decoder or encoder-only scoring) — low token lengths, high QPS
  - Embedding lookups for similarity and index refreshes — short inputs, parallelized
  - Multiturn conversational assistant — small prompts but moderate responses and KV cache reuse

SLOs: 95th pct p99 latency goal for gen responses < 350ms (token streaming acceptable), rerank scoring p99 < 75ms. Cost is a factor; we want to understand tradeoffs between Dedicated vs. hosted burst lanes.

Can you run a preliminary sizing and recommended config for Dedicated capacity (GPU types, node counts, suggested batching and cache settings) that account for the burst windows? Happy to hop on a quick call as well — Jim (cc) can join.

Attachments: sample CSV of token distribution (will follow), sample prompt set forthcoming.

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Platform Engineering
Atlas Retail

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Sizing kickoff — Atlas inference footprint (flash sale / holiday burst)

Ava / Marissa — quick first-pass sizing and assumptions. This is a hypothesis to validate with a short profiling run using their sample prompts.

Assumptions:
- Primary generative model for chat: ~7B dense-ish variant (approx 7–13B effective FP16 params) — target 8–12ms per token on a single H100 stream with optimized kernels (ballpark).
- Rerank workload: encoder-only model 700M–2B with low token lengths; high QPS but very low per-request cost when batched
- Embeddings: quantized 8-bit runs, low perf penalty, high parallel throughput
- Average tokens per gen call: request 40 in + 120 out = ~160 tokens total
- Effective throughput per GPU (H100-80GB) for mixed workload with continuous batching & KV reuse: approx 1,200–1,600 tokens/sec for gen-heavy lanes; A100-80GB noted lower but still reasonable for cost optimization

Sizing options (baseline + burst headroom):
1) Cost-optimized: 8 x A100-80GB nodes (baseline pool) + hosted burst lanes. Estimated baseline sustained capacity: ~800–1,200 gen req/s (with batching tuned). For Atlas's 1.8k sustained spike this requires relying on hosted overflow for the peak 600–1k req/s burst.

2) Performance-first (recommended if p99 SLO is critical): 10 x H100-80GB dedicated nodes configured with continuous batching, prioritized low-latency lanes for rerank. Estimated sustained capacity: ~1.8k gen+rerank req/s with careful batching windows (~30–60ms), and headroom for short bursts to 2.5–3.0k with optimized pre-warming and prefix cache.

3) Hybrid high-availability: 6 x H100 baseline for steady-state + an autoscale policy (burst pool) that can spin up additional H100 capacity from a reserved pool when telemetry shows crossing thresholds. This reduces monthly commit but requires coordination on burst SLA and fallback behavior.

Operational suggestions:
- Enable KV/prefix caching for conversational flows to reduce repeated token compute (can cut gen token work by ~35–60% depending on prompt reuse).
- Per-route batch size caps and latency-aware batching to meet p99 targets; rerank routes should use very small batches (<8) and priority scheduling.
- Pre-warm tokenizers and maintain hot model instances for the top-5 most-used model variants to reduce cold-start jitter.
- Run a 2-hour synthetic soak with their sample prompts to validate tail behavior; collect p50/p95/p99 and token-level throughput.

Back-of-envelope monthly commit estimate (in GPU-nodes):
- Option 1: 8 A100 nodes
- Option 2 (rec): 10 H100 nodes
- Option 3: 6 H100 baseline + burst capacity

I'll draft a short spreadsheet with throughput math (tokens/sec per GPU, effective requests/sec by workload mix) and attach. Recommend we get their sample prompts and token CSV to tighten numbers.

— Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Elena / Jim — thanks again for the numbers and the quick turnaround from the Atlas team. Attached is a short token profile you mentioned plus our initial estimate (spreadsheet). Summary of our recommended next steps: 

1) Short profiler run: Atlas sends a ~30–60 minute sample trace (we'll provide an ingestion script); Dev will run the workload on both H100 and A100 instances to measure effective tokens/sec and tail latency.
2) If p99 <350ms is a hard requirement during bursts, we should aim for the performance-first config (10 x H100-80GB) as the committed baseline or a hybrid with explicit burst lanes.
3) Configure per-route SLOs in the Redwood Console and enable KV/prefix caching for the conversational flows prior to the event.
4) Decide on burst SLA: 1) host fallback overflow (lowest commit), 2) reserved burst pool (medium), or 3) commit to enough Dedicated nodes for the absolute peak (highest cost).
